applicable_when: The kernel is a pure layout-permutation (transpose) over a (256,128,3,3) tensor. It launches 4096 blocks on 132 SMs, producing 1 full wave (~2112 blocks) plus a partial wave of ~1984 blocks. NCU's LaunchConfiguration rule estimates up to 50% runtime is spent in this tail. The root cause is YBLOCK=8 being too small: ynumel=32768 / YBLOCK=8 = 4096 CTAs in Y, while XBLOCK=128 covers xnumel=9 in a single CTA. Increasing YBLOCK to 32 or 64 reduces the Y-dimension CTA count to 1024 or 512, collapsing the grid to 1024 or 512 blocks, well within 1 full wave on 132 SMs (132x16=2112 max). This eliminates the partial wave entirely. Additionally, larger YBLOCK tiles improve L1 cache reuse for the strided loads (currently only 18/32 bytes per sector utilized). Adding @triton.autotune explores the optimal (XBLOCK, YBLOCK, num_warps) combination automatically.
